notes:
Repeated neutral locators do not distinguish individual component tests; identical locators are treated consistently without assigning tests by input order. Original-side values quoted by replication authors were not substituted for the unavailable original primary source. Replication d and p come from the same relative-liking test in the primary write-up. Final author table row 29 gives F(1,593)=0.002 whereas write-up prints F=0.001; discrepancy retained, no averaging or conversion. Both identify N=595. Choice-share Mann–Whitney test is a separate outcome, not combined with the relative-liking d. No explicit narrative replication-success verdict located. 
Source follow-up: Fresh blind validation of original side only. Verified supplied title and authors against the named canonical text and rendered PDF pages 5–6 (printed main-article pp. 17–18). All three assigned records have identical original study, description, page locator and requested metric; their audit_id or order cannot establish distinct tests. On main-article p. 18 (PDF p. 6), the relative-liking ANOVA reports F(1, 198) = 3.80, p = .05; the separate favorite-choice-share Mann–Whitney test reports Z = –2.20, p = .028. Exact canonical-text snippets respectively: "cant main effect (F(1, 198) = 3.80, p = .05)." and "the supply of each item (ZMann–Whitney = –2.20, p = .028) as". Both tests fit the supplied description. Nearby analyses of variety and popularity and a footnote on absolute liking are additional distinct tests, not interchangeable with these outcomes. No unique per-record test assignment is possible from the allowed input, so statistic fields remain null rather than selecting a test by input order. Main-article p. 17 (PDF p. 5) reports two hundred participants for the main experiment and a separate 80-person pretest; the one-person exclusion on p. 18 applies specifically to popularity ratings. The exact analytic sample for an unresolved target is therefore not entered. The rendered page confirms the numeric meanings and signs of the candidate tests; the canonical text flattens the Z subscript and line-breaks the ANOVA sentence, and the exact quote fragments preserve those features rather than normalizing them. Published main article pp. 13–26 ends at PDF p. 14; the separately paginated Web Appendix starts at PDF p. 15 and was not used to establish missing main-article fields. Replication and narrative success are unassigned placeholders.
